title: Threat modelling an LLM application: trust boundaries and data flows

videos.script: A threat model starts with a drawing. {{title}} Tarefa's assistant has ten components. They sit in three zones: the internet, Tarefa's own servers, and the company that runs the model. {{zones}} Where two zones meet there is a trust boundary. Six of the twelve flows cross one, and each crossing is a question somebody has to answer. {{crossing}} Then a second lens. Who wrote the text in each flow? An attachment never leaves Tarefa's servers. But a client wrote it, and the model reads it beside Tarefa's instructions. {{text}} Every flow that matters gets the same six questions, one for each letter of STRIDE. {{stride}} The answers go into a register, ranked by impact times likelihood, with the control that answers each threat. {{register}} Three entries have no control yet. And two flows have no entry at all. That is the gap a list cannot see in itself, and the program checks for it. {{gaps}}
